questions.questionMarkup: Which of the following is the correct order of the five project management process group?
questions.questionText: Which of the following is the correct order of the five project management process group?

options.html: Initiating → Planning → Executing → Monitoring and Controlling → Closing
options.text: Initiating → Planning → Executing → Monitoring and Controlling → Closing

options.html: Planning → Initiating → Executing → Monitoring and Controlling → Closing
options.text: Planning → Initiating → Executing → Monitoring and Controlling → Closing

options.html: Initiating → Planning → Monitoring and Controlling → Executing → Closing
options.text: Initiating → Planning → Monitoring and Controlling → Executing → Closing

options.html: Executing → Planning → Initiating → Monitoring and Controlling → Closing
options.text: Executing → Planning → Initiating → Monitoring and Controlling → Closing

questions.explanationHtml:
(a)
The project management process groups that provide a structured approach to project management.
Five key project management processes order
1. Initiating process group.
2. Planning process group.
3. Execution process group.
4. Monitoring and controlling process group.
5. Closing process group.
This sequence is critical because it establishes a logical flow, starting with formal authorization
and planning moving through execution and monitoring with project closure.

questions.subject: Civil Engineering
questions.questionMarkup:
Which of the following statements about risk management are correct?
1. Risk avoidance involves completely eliminating the risk from the project.
2. Risk mitigation means reducing either the probability or impact of a risk.
3. Risk acceptance requires no action and assumes the project will not be affected by the risk.
4. Risk transfer is always the best strategy for managing financial risk.
questions.questionText: Which of the following statements about risk management are correct? 1. Risk avoidance involves completely eliminating the risk from the project. 2. Risk mitigation means reducing either the probability or impact of a risk. 3. Risk acceptance requires no action and assumes the project will not be affected by the risk. 4. Risk transfer is always the best strategy for managing financial risk.
questions.explanationHtml:
(c)
• Risk acceptance does not mean no action or no effect.
• Risk transfer is not always the best strategy.

questions.subject: Civil Engineering
questions.questionMarkup: In team development, which of the following represents the correct sequence of stages a project team undergoes according to Tuckman’s model?
questions.questionText: In team development, which of the following represents the correct sequence of stages a project team undergoes according to Tuckman’s model?
questions.explanationHtml:
(d)
Tuckman’s five stages of team development describe how team evolve and improve their effectiveness over time.
• Forming : Team members get to know each other, roles are unclear and initial relationships are established.
• Storming : Conflicts arise as team members assert their opinions and vie for roles.
• Norming : The team begins to develop cohesion, resolve conflicts and establish norms.
• Performing : The team reaches peak efficiency, collaboration is strong and goals are achieved smoothly.
• Adjourning : The project ends and the team disbands or transitions.

questions.explanationHtml:
(b)
